Almost everyone who makes the claim that socialism can work like to cite Scandinavia as an example. However, Scandinavia is not the same as America.

The Nordic citizens generally all have the same interests and needs. About 80% of citizens there have Scandinavian-born parents, so racial needs are the same for everyone, for example. Everyone wants liberalism and socialism there as well, so everyone agrees to the same places to spend money. Compare this to America, a country that is diverse racially, ideologically, and culturally. Everyone will need something different. People in the Rust Belt, for example, have different needs from people in Silicon Valley. A guy who works in a steel plant in Ohio doesn't want his taxes to be spent on a hyperloop transit system he will never use in California. Conversely, a San Francisco resident doesn't want their money to be spent on investments in Ohio's steel plants. Socialism, running under only one powerful government, has a one-size-fits-all system that can't properly serve America, and dictates that everyone in the cities pays the same high taxes as the farmers who have only a little money that goes further in their neck of the woods, all to fund the same hyperloop in Cali they won't ever use. Capitalism (without monopolies), on the other hand, caters to many different groups of people. You have multiple companies to choose from with many different products, so you can find the product that suits your needs the best, and skip the ones you don't need and make your dollar count the most. Decentralized governments/Federalism also works well for diverse cultures and ideologies, which is why we use Federalism here in America. The citizens of Ohio can invest their taxes into their steel infrastructure, while Cali citizens can invest their money towards tech innovations, and everyone is happy.
